1926.claim: Robert Goddard launches the world's first liquid-fueled rocket at Auburn, Massachusetts.
NBC launches as the first permanent national radio broadcasting network in the US.

1927.claim: Charles Lindbergh completes the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight (New York–Paris) in the Spirit of St. Louis.
Philo Farnsworth demonstrates the first working all-electronic television image transmission.
The Jazz Singer premieres as the first feature-length film with synchronized recorded dialogue, launching the sound-film era.

1928.claim: The Northern Expedition ends with nominal national reunification under the Nationalist (KMT) government seated at Nanjing.
Academia Sinica (中央研究院), China's national academy of sciences, is founded at Nanjing.
The Central Bank of China is established in Shanghai as the Nationalist government's central bank.

1929.claim: Pei Wenzhong discovers the first Peking Man (Homo erectus) skullcap at Zhoukoudian.

1930.claim: China completes the restoration of tariff autonomy as the last major power accedes, ending foreign control over Chinese customs tariff rates. Anchor justification: treaty sequence US 1928 -> most powers by end-1928 -> new tariff effective Feb 1929 -> Japan (last major power) 6 May 1930; anchored to the 1930 completion.
Clyde Tombaugh discovers Pluto at Lowell Observatory, the first trans-Neptunian object found.

1931.claim: Liang Shuming establishes the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute at Zouping, a landmark rural-reconstruction and mass-education experiment.
The Empire State Building is completed in New York City, then the tallest building in the world (381 m).
Ernest Lawrence builds the first working cyclotron at Berkeley, enabling particle acceleration.

1932.claim: By ~1932 the Rong family's Shenxin cotton mills were China's largest industrial employer (~31,700 workers across nine mills, roughly a fifth of Chinese-owned spindles); with the Maoxin/Fuxin flour mills the Rong group was the country's largest private industrial enterprise - the 'flour and textile kings'.

1933.claim: China's 'abolish the tael, adopt the yuan' reform standardizes the silver dollar (yuan) as the national monetary unit, replacing the tael.
The Tennessee Valley Authority is established, a federal authority for regional electrification and river development.
The Glass–Steagall Banking Act creates federal deposit insurance (FDIC) and separates commercial and investment banking.

1935.claim: The fabi (法币) currency reform abandons the silver standard and unifies a managed national paper currency.
The Chinese Communist Party's Red Army completes the Long March, consolidating Mao Zedong's leadership and the CCP's survival.
The Social Security Act establishes national old-age pensions and unemployment insurance.
Hoover Dam on the Colorado River is completed, then the world's largest concrete structure and hydroelectric dam.
Wallace Carothers's team at DuPont first synthesizes nylon, the first fully synthetic polymer fiber.
The Douglas DC-3 makes its first flight, becoming the airliner that made passenger air travel commercially viable.

1936.claim: The Canton-Hankow (Yuehan) Railway is completed, linking Guangzhou to Wuhan as a major north-south trunk line.

1937.claim: The Qiantang River Bridge at Hangzhou, chief-engineered by Mao Yisheng, opens as the first modern double-deck road-and-rail bridge designed and built by Chinese engineers.
The Golden Gate Bridge opens in San Francisco, then the world's longest suspension-bridge main span.

1938.claim: The National Southwestern Associated University (Xinan Lianda) forms in Kunming, merging Peking, Tsinghua, and Nankai universities to preserve higher education through the war.
The Chinese Industrial Cooperatives ('Gung Ho') movement organizes decentralized wartime production across the interior.

The Yunnan section of the Burma Road (Kunming to Wanting at the Burmese border, ~960 km), built by an estimated 200,000 Chinese laborers under Nationalist direction, opens to motor traffic in 1938. [Alt anchor: formal completion sometimes dated 1939; both recorded. Narrowed to the Chinese-built Yunnan section per batch-3 ruling.]

The Yichang evacuation (Oct-Dec 1938): Lu Zuofu's Minsheng Shipping Company moves 30,000+ people and ~100,000 tons of supplies - including key industrial equipment - up the Yangtze through the Three Gorges to Sichuan in about 40 days before Yichang's fall, saving much of China's wartime industrial base (the 'Dunkirk of Chinese industry').
Chester Carlson produces the first xerographic image, inventing electrophotography (later Xerox copying).

1939.claim: Hewlett-Packard is founded in Palo Alto, an origin point of what became Silicon Valley.

1942.claim: Enrico Fermi's team achieves the first controlled, self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction (Chicago Pile-1).
Grand Coulee Dam on the Columbia River is completed, the largest concrete structure and hydroelectric plant in the US.
Over 1942-1945, US wartime industrial mobilization mass-produces war materiel at unprecedented scale (~300,000 aircraft and ~2,700 Liberty ships across the war).

1943.claim: The US and UK relinquish extraterritorial rights in China by treaty, ending a century of the 'unequal treaties'.
US pharmaceutical firms achieve deep-tank fermentation mass production of penicillin, enabling the first antibiotic at scale.

1944.claim: The Bretton Woods conference establishes the IMF and the framework for the World Bank, anchoring the postwar monetary order.
The GI Bill (Servicemen's Readjustment Act) funds mass higher education and home ownership for returning veterans.

1945.claim: China becomes a founding member of the United Nations and a permanent member of the Security Council.
ENIAC, the first general-purpose electronic digital computer, becomes operational.
The Manhattan Project achieves the first nuclear detonation (Trinity test), demonstrating engineered nuclear fission at scale.
Vannevar Bush's report 'Science, the Endless Frontier' sets the blueprint for federal funding of basic research (leading to the NSF).

1946.claim: American Research and Development Corporation (ARD) is founded (Georges Doriot, Karl Compton, Ralph Flanders) - the first modern institutional venture-capital firm, raising outside capital to fund new companies; its 1957 investment of $70,000 for ~70% of Digital Equipment Corporation grew to ~$355 million by 1971.

1947.claim: Bell Labs invents the point-contact transistor (Bardeen, Brattain, Shockley), foundation of all modern electronics.
Chuck Yeager pilots the Bell X-1 to the first crewed supersonic flight, breaking the sound barrier.
Levittown, New York begins mass-produced suburban housing, a template for postwar American suburbanization.

1948.claim: The Marshall Plan (European Recovery Program) begins large-scale US-funded reconstruction of Western Europe.
Claude Shannon publishes 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication', founding information theory.

1949.claim: The People's Republic of China is founded, ending decades of civil war and fragmentation on the mainland.
The US leads the founding of NATO, the postwar transatlantic security institution.

1950.claim: The Marriage Law of 1950 bans arranged and child marriage and establishes new legal rights for women.
Nationwide Land Reform (1950-1953) redistributes land from landlords to peasants under the 1950 Agrarian Reform Law.
The new government halts hyperinflation and stabilizes the renminbi, restoring monetary order.

1951.claim: UNIVAC I is delivered as the first commercially produced electronic computer in the US.

1952.claim: The Patriotic Health Campaign mobilizes mass sanitation and disease-control drives nationwide.
The US detonates 'Ivy Mike', the first full-scale thermonuclear (hydrogen) device.

1953.claim: The First Five-Year Plan (1953-1957) begins Soviet-aided heavy industrialization built around 156 key projects.

China conducts its first modern national census, counting roughly 583 million people. [Conflicting figures recorded: official count 582.6M (1953) vs the prior ~450M League of Nations 1933 estimate; G. Cressey questioned the count as inflated, though later scholarship assessed ~100% coverage.]
The NTSC color television standard is adopted, launching compatible color broadcasting in the US.

1954.claim: The first Constitution of the PRC is adopted and the first National People's Congress convenes.
USS Nautilus is commissioned as the world's first nuclear-powered submarine.
Bell Labs demonstrates the first practical silicon solar cell.

1955.claim: Qian Xuesen returns from the US to China, seeding the country's missile and later space programs.
Jonas Salk's inactivated polio vaccine is licensed after mass field trials, curbing a feared epidemic disease.
Ray Kroc launches the McDonald's franchise system, a template for standardized mass-service industry.

1956.claim: The First Automobile Works produces the Jiefang CA-10 truck, the first motor vehicle manufactured in China.
The 'socialist transformation' of industry and commerce is completed, converting private enterprise to public/joint ownership.
China's State Council promulgates the first Scheme for Simplifying Chinese Characters (515 simplified characters plus 54 radicals), a mass-literacy language reform.
The Federal-Aid Highway Act launches the Interstate Highway System, the largest US public-works program.
IBM ships the RAMAC 305, the first computer with a moving-head hard disk drive.

1957.claim: The Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opens, the first bridge to span the Yangtze, carrying rail and road.
The Shippingport Atomic Power Station begins operation as the first full-scale commercial nuclear power plant in the United States.

1958.claim: Hanyu Pinyin romanization is adopted, complementing simplified characters in a national literacy drive.
NASA is established as the US civilian space agency.
Explorer 1, the first US satellite, reaches orbit and discovers the Van Allen radiation belts.
Jack Kilby at Texas Instruments demonstrates the first integrated circuit.
The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (ARPA/DARPA) is established, seeding foundational US technologies (packet networking, GPS, stealth, autonomy).

The Boeing 707 enters commercial service with Pan Am, inaugurating the jet age of mass commercial air travel. [Commercial service began 26 Oct 1958 (Pan Am); prototype first flight 20 Dec 1957 recorded as alternative anchor.]

1959.claim: The Daqing oilfield is discovered, launching China's path to petroleum self-sufficiency. [Era context: within the Great Leap Forward (1958-1962) - context, not adjudication; oil self-sufficiency (~1963) a later consequence.]

The Great Hall of the People and the 'Ten Great Buildings' are completed for the PRC's tenth anniversary. [Era context: one of the Great Leap Forward's 'Ten Great Buildings', realised in ~10 months by ~8,000 workers.]
The Xerox 914, the first successful plain-paper office copier, is introduced, commercializing xerography at scale.
The Convair SM-65 Atlas, the first operational US intercontinental ballistic missile, entered service in 1959, with the first squadron on combat alert at Vandenberg AFB on 31 October 1959.

1960.claim: Theodore Maiman operates the first working laser.
The FDA approves the first oral contraceptive pill. [Contraceptive indication approved 1960 (Enovid was approved for other indications 1957); this row's anchor is the 1960 contraceptive approval.]

1961.claim: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space aboard a Mercury capsule.
The first Unimate industrial robot is installed on a General Motors assembly line (Ewing Township, New Jersey), inaugurating industrial robotics.

1962.claim: Telstar 1, the first active communications satellite, relays the first live transatlantic television.

1964.claim: China detonates its first atomic bomb, becoming the fifth nuclear-weapons state.

The 'Third Front' program begins building a dispersed heavy-industrial base in China's interior. [Event = program launched May 1964; cumulative 1964-1980 scale per scholarship: ~205bn yuan, 11M+ people relocated, 1,100+ projects (magnitude noted; event is the anchor).]
IBM introduces the System/360, the first compatible family of mainframe computers.
The Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlaws discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.

1965.claim: Chinese scientists achieve the first total synthesis of crystalline bovine insulin, the first synthesis of a functional protein.
The Voting Rights Act of 1965 bans racial discrimination in voting.
Medicare and Medicaid are created, establishing federal health coverage for the elderly and poor.

1967.claim: China detonates its first hydrogen bomb, only 32 months after its first atomic test.

1968.claim: The Nanjing Yangtze River Bridge opens, the first Yangtze bridge designed and built entirely by China.

The 'barefoot doctors' program scales basic rural healthcare to hundreds of millions. [Event = program endorsed/scaled 1968 during the Cultural Revolution (era context); reached ~1.5M barefoot doctors covering ~90% of villages by 1978 (magnitude); cited for the 1978 WHO Alma-Ata Declaration.]
Intel is founded, the company that would commercialize the microprocessor and lead the semiconductor industry.

1969.claim: The Red Flag Canal, a ~1,500 km hand-built irrigation system diverting the Zhang River through the Taihang Mountains at Linzhou (Lin County), Henan, is completed. [Completion: main canal 1965, full system July 1969 (anchor); event established by independent scholarship. The official 'tenfold food production' magnitude and 'Eighth Wonder / self-reliance' framing are state-mythologized and NOT independently verified - recorded as such (event/magnitude split). Era context: initiated ~1960, hand-built through the hard post-Great-Leap years (81 workers died).]
Apollo 11 lands the first humans on the Moon.
ARPANET carries its first host-to-host message, the direct ancestor of the internet.
Bell Labs develops the Unix operating system.

1970.claim: China launches its first satellite, Dong Fang Hong 1, becoming the fifth nation to reach orbit.
The Boeing 747 enters commercial service, inaugurating the wide-body jumbo-jet era.
The Environmental Protection Agency is created and the Clean Air Act is strengthened.

1971.claim: The PRC takes China's United Nations seat, including permanent Security Council membership.
Intel ships the 4004, the first commercially available microprocessor.
The US ends dollar-gold convertibility (the 'Nixon shock'), collapsing the Bretton Woods fixed-rate system.
NASDAQ launches as the first electronic stock market.
FedEx is founded, pioneering the hub-and-spoke overnight-delivery logistics industry.
Ray Tomlinson sends the first networked email across ARPANET, establishing the user@host addressing convention.

1972.claim: Tu Youyou's team isolates artemisinin (qinghaosu), a highly effective antimalarial, under Project 523. [Isolation of qinghaosu/artemisinin, 8 Nov 1972 (Project 523); Nobel Prize 2015.]
President Nixon's visit and the Shanghai Communiqué begin US-China rapprochement.
Pioneer 10 launches, becoming the first spacecraft to traverse the asteroid belt and fly by Jupiter.
Atari is founded and releases Pong, launching the commercial video-game industry.
Dennis Ritchie creates the C programming language at Bell Labs, a foundational systems-programming language.

1973.claim: Yuan Longping's team achieves the first high-yield hybrid rice, a major advance for food security. [First three-line high-yield hybrid (Nanyou 2), 1973; ~20% yield gain independently corroborated (IRRI/Wiley); large-scale cultivation from 1976.]
Cohen and Boyer demonstrate practical recombinant DNA, founding genetic engineering and biotechnology.
Robert Metcalfe invents Ethernet at Xerox PARC.
Motorola's Martin Cooper places the first handheld cellular phone call.

1974.claim: The Terracotta Army is discovered near Xi'an, one of the century's great archaeological finds.
China commissions its first nuclear-powered submarine (Type 091 'Long March 1'), the first indigenously built nuclear attack submarine in Asia.
The first UPC barcode is scanned on a commercial product (a pack of gum at a Marsh supermarket, Troy, Ohio), inaugurating automated retail scanning.

1975.claim: China launches and recovers its first returnable satellite, the third nation to achieve satellite recovery.
The Altair 8800 sparks the personal-computer movement and Microsoft is founded.

1976.claim: The Cultural Revolution ends with Mao Zedong's death and the arrest of the Gang of Four.
Apple is founded and the Apple II (1977) helps launch the personal-computer industry.
Seymour Cray's Cray-1 defines the modern supercomputer.
Genentech is founded, the first biotechnology company, launching the industry.

1977.claim: The national college entrance examination (gaokao) is restored and universities reopen.
NASA launches Voyager 1 and 2 on a grand tour of the outer planets.
The Atari 2600 popularizes the cartridge-based home video-game console.
The first whole-body MRI scan is performed, launching magnetic-resonance medical imaging.

1978.claim: Reform and Opening is launched at the Third Plenum, beginning China's market-oriented transformation.
The Household Responsibility System decollectivizes agriculture, sharply raising farm output and rural incomes.
Over 1978-2019, reform-era growth lifts roughly 800 million Chinese out of extreme poverty (World Bank international poverty line) - one of the largest poverty reductions in recorded history.

Xu Guangxian ('father of Chinese rare-earth chemistry') developed a countercurrent/cascade solvent-extraction theory for rare-earth separation in the 1970s, providing the design basis for industrial-scale separation of individual rare-earth elements; recognized with China's State Preeminent Science and Technology Award (2008).
The first GPS (Navstar) satellite is launched, beginning the global positioning system.

1979.claim: The US and China establish full diplomatic relations.

1980.claim: China establishes its first Special Economic Zones, with Shenzhen as the flagship.
China joins the IMF and the World Bank, rejoining the core global economic institutions.
China introduces the one-child policy, a sweeping state intervention in fertility.
The Bayh-Dole Act and Genentech's IPO catalyze university tech-transfer and the biotechnology industry.

1981.claim: IBM introduces the IBM PC, standardizing the personal-computer platform.
The Space Shuttle Columbia makes the first flight of a reusable crewed spacecraft.

1982.claim: Surgeons implant the Jarvik-7, the first permanent artificial heart in a human.

The Small Business Innovation Development Act of 1982 establishes the Small Business Innovation Research (SBIR) program, mandating that federal agencies set aside a share of their extramural R&D budgets for small businesses - federal seed funding that seeded later deep-technology firms.

1983.claim: China completes Yinhe-I (Galaxy-1), its first domestically built supercomputer.
ARPANET switches to TCP/IP, the moment usually called the birth of the internet.

1984.claim: Lenovo (Legend) and Haier are founded, among the first globally competitive Chinese technology and consumer firms.
China opens fourteen coastal cities to foreign investment, widening the reform beyond the SEZs.
Apple's Macintosh brings the graphical user interface and mouse to a mass consumer market.
Cisco Systems is founded, becoming the dominant vendor of internet-networking equipment.

1985.claim: China establishes Great Wall Station, its first Antarctic research base.
Microsoft releases Windows 1.0, beginning its dominant PC graphical operating environment.

1986.claim: China launches the '863 Program', a national high-technology R&D initiative.
NSFNET establishes a national backbone that scales the internet toward public use.

1987.claim: Huawei is founded in Shenzhen, later becoming the world's largest telecommunications-equipment maker and a 5G leader.

1988.claim: The Beijing Electron-Positron Collider begins operation, China's first major high-energy physics facility.
Hainan becomes a province and China's largest Special Economic Zone.
Over 1988-2011, China builds out a national expressway network from its first expressway (1988) to the world's longest, surpassing the US Interstate Highway System in 2011 (~84,000 km).
TAT-8, the first transatlantic fiber-optic telecommunications cable, enters service.
The first commercial 3D printer (stereolithography) ships, launching additive manufacturing.

1989.claim: The Lockheed F-117 Nighthawk - the world's first operational stealth combat aircraft (initial operational capability October 1983, publicly acknowledged 1988) - flew its first combat missions during the US invasion of Panama on 19-20 December 1989.

1990.claim: The Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges open, restoring equity markets in China.
China launches development of the Pudong New Area, transforming Shanghai into a global financial hub.
China hosts the Beijing Asian Games, its first large international multi-sport event.
The Hubble Space Telescope is launched, transforming observational astronomy.
The Human Genome Project begins, the US-led international effort to sequence human DNA.

1991.claim: The Qinshan Nuclear Power Plant, China's first domestically designed nuclear station, connects to the grid.

1992.claim: Deng Xiaoping's Southern Tour reaccelerates reform; the '14th Party Congress' adopts the 'socialist market economy'.

1993.claim: The NCSA Mosaic browser makes the World Wide Web usable and ignites its explosive growth.

1994.claim: China enacts tax-sharing fiscal reform and unifies its exchange rate, foundations of its high-growth era.
China establishes full internet connectivity with a first TCP/IP link to the global network.
Netscape and Amazon are founded, launching the commercial web and e-commerce.
NAFTA takes effect, creating a continental free-trade area.

1995.claim: BYD is founded, later becoming the world's largest manufacturer of electric and new-energy vehicles.
Microsoft releases Windows 95, bringing modern GUI computing to the mass market.
Sun releases Java, a write-once-run-anywhere programming platform for the networked era.
GPS reaches full operational capability, providing global positioning as public infrastructure.
eBay is founded, pioneering large-scale online marketplaces.

1997.claim: Hong Kong (1997) and Macau (1999) return to Chinese sovereignty under 'one country, two systems'.
IBM's Deep Blue defeats world chess champion Garry Kasparov, a landmark for machine intelligence.
Mars Pathfinder lands and deploys Sojourner, the first successful Mars rover.

1998.claim: Google is founded, reorganizing access to the world's information around search.
Assembly of the International Space Station begins, the largest crewed structure in orbit.

1999.claim: Tencent (1998), Alibaba (1999), and Baidu (2000) are founded, the core of China's internet economy.
BGI (Beijing Genomics Institute) is founded, later among the world's largest genome-sequencing organizations.
iFlytek is founded, a leading Chinese speech-recognition and AI company.

2000.claim: China launches the Western Development Strategy to industrialize and connect its interior.

2001.claim: China accedes to the World Trade Organization, integrating into the global trading system.
China becomes the world's largest mobile-phone market by subscribers.
Hikvision is founded, growing into the world's largest maker of video-surveillance equipment.
Wikipedia launches, creating the largest collaborative reference work in history.
Apple releases the iPod, reshaping digital music and consumer devices.

An MQ-1 Predator fired a Hellfire missile for the first time on 16 February 2001 at a US test range; armed Predators conducted their first operational combat strikes in Afghanistan in autumn 2001, inaugurating armed-drone warfare.

2002.claim: China becomes the world's largest recipient of foreign direct investment.
SpaceX is founded, catalyzing low-cost, reusable commercial spaceflight.

2003.claim: Shenzhou 5 carries Yang Liwei to orbit, China's first crewed spaceflight.
China completes its ~1% share of the Human Genome Project, the only developing country in the consortium.
The Human Genome Project is completed, delivering an essentially finished human reference genome.
Tesla is founded, helping launch the modern electric-vehicle industry.

2004.claim: Facebook is founded, launching the era of mass social networking.
NASA lands the Spirit and Opportunity rovers on Mars for long-duration exploration.

2005.claim: Lenovo acquires IBM's personal-computer division, an emblematic Chinese firm going global.
YouTube is founded, creating mass online video and the creator economy.

2006.claim: The Qinghai-Tibet Railway opens, the highest railway in the world.
The Three Gorges Dam is completed as the world's largest hydroelectric power station.
DJI is founded, later dominating the global consumer and commercial drone market.
Amazon Web Services launches, creating the modern cloud-computing industry.

2007.claim: China launches Chang'e 1, its first lunar orbiter.
Apple releases the iPhone, defining the modern smartphone.

2008.claim: China hosts the Beijing Summer Olympics, a landmark of national arrival and infrastructure.
The Beijing-Tianjin intercity line opens, launching China's high-speed rail network.
SpaceX's Falcon 1 becomes the first privately developed liquid-fueled rocket to reach orbit.
Apple's App Store launches, creating the mobile-application economy.
Google's Android launches, becoming the world's dominant mobile operating system.
Over ~2008-2018, the shale revolution (hydraulic fracturing and horizontal drilling) makes the US the world's largest producer of natural gas (by 2011) and crude oil (by 2018).

2010.claim: China becomes the world's second-largest economy, surpassing Japan.
China becomes the world's largest manufacturing nation and merchandise exporter.
Xiaomi is founded, later a top-tier global smartphone and consumer-electronics / IoT maker.

Over 2010-2023, China rose to hold more than 80% of global manufacturing CAPACITY at every stage of the crystalline-silicon solar PV supply chain (polysilicon, ingots, wafers, cells, modules), reaching 97% of wafer capacity, up from roughly 50-80% per stage in 2010.

Over 2010-2024 China consolidated dominance of global commercial shipbuilding: it overtook South Korea to become the world's largest shipbuilder by deadweight-tonnage completions in 2010 (having passed Japan in 2009), and by 2023 delivered more than half of the world's ship output for the first time, reaching about 53.8% of global gross tonnage in 2024 (South Korea ~27%, Japan ~13%).
Craig Venter's team builds the first cell controlled by a synthetic genome.
The Affordable Care Act expands US health-insurance coverage.

2011.claim: CATL is founded, later becoming the world's largest maker of electric-vehicle batteries.
China launches Tiangong-1, its first space laboratory and orbital docking target.
IBM's Watson defeats champions at Jeopardy!, showcasing natural-language AI.

2012.claim: ByteDance is founded, later creating Douyin/TikTok, the first Chinese consumer-internet platform to reach mass global scale.

China commissioned its first aircraft carrier, Liaoning (a refit of the ex-Soviet Varyag), on 25 September 2012, and conducted its first fixed-wing (J-15) arrested carrier landings in November 2012 - the start of Chinese carrier aviation.

China fielded the road-mobile DF-21D (from ~2010-2012) and later DF-26 anti-ship-capable ballistic missiles, which IISS lists in the PLA Rocket Force order of battle. Their effectiveness against maneuvering warships at sea is asserted by US defense assessments but has not been independently demonstrated in open sources.
NASA lands the Curiosity rover on Mars for long-duration science.
Doudna and Charpentier demonstrate programmable CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing.

2013.claim: Chang'e 3 and the Yutu rover achieve China's first soft landing on the Moon.
Tianhe-2 becomes the world's fastest supercomputer.

China became the world's largest market for industrial robots in 2013 (world's #1 in annual installations) and has led every year since - installing 295,000 of the 542,000 industrial robots deployed worldwide in 2024 (54%, more than the rest of the world combined).

2014.claim: China's high-speed rail network becomes the world's largest, exceeding the rest of the world combined.
Alibaba's IPO becomes the largest in history to that point, marking China's internet economy on the world stage.
Over ~2014-2018, mobile payments (Alipay and WeChat Pay) become the dominant consumer payment method in China, largely bypassing payment cards.
NIO is founded, a premium Chinese electric-vehicle maker.
SenseTime is founded, a leading Chinese computer-vision and AI company.

2015.claim: Tu Youyou wins the Nobel Prize in Medicine for artemisinin, China's first science Nobel for work done in China.
SpaceX lands an orbital rocket's first stage, proving reusable launch vehicles.
LIGO makes the first direct detection of gravitational waves.
The US Supreme Court establishes a nationwide right to same-sex marriage (Obergefell).

2016.claim: China launches Micius, the world's first quantum-communications satellite.
China completes FAST, the world's largest single-dish radio telescope.
China's Long March 5 heavy-lift rocket makes its maiden flight, enabling later space-station, lunar-sample, and Mars missions.

2017.claim: China's C919, its first domestically developed large passenger jet, makes its maiden flight.

CATL became the world's largest EV/lithium-ion battery maker by installed capacity in 2017, overtaking Panasonic, and has held the #1 global position every year through 2025 - reaching about 37.9% global share in 2024 and 39.2% in 2025.

The Chengdu J-20 'Mighty Dragon' stealth fighter, first flown in 2011, entered PLA Air Force service around 2017 and has since been fielded in operational units - the first stealth fighter outside the United States to reach operational service.
Google researchers publish the Transformer architecture ('Attention Is All You Need'), the basis of modern large language models.

The US Navy commissioned USS Gerald R. Ford (CVN-78) on 22 July 2017 - the lead ship of the first new US aircraft-carrier class in over four decades (since the Nimitz class) and the first carrier to use an electromagnetic aircraft-launch system (EMALS) and Advanced Arresting Gear; it made its first operational deployment in 2023.

2018.claim: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge opens as the world's longest sea-crossing.
SpaceX flies the Falcon Heavy, the most powerful operational rocket of its time, with reusable boosters.

2019.claim: Chang'e 4 makes the first-ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon.
China begins commercial 5G and builds the world's largest 5G network.
Beijing Daxing International Airport opens, among the world's largest single-terminal airports.
Huawei releases HarmonyOS (2019), its own operating system; early versions were AOSP-compatible, and a fully Android-independent version, HarmonyOS NEXT, followed in 2024.

2020.claim: China declares the elimination of extreme rural poverty, lifting the last counties above its poverty line.
Chang'e 5 returns lunar samples to Earth, the first sample return since 1976.
China completes the BeiDou-3 global satellite navigation system, an independent alternative to GPS.

BYD launched the Blade battery - a cell-to-pack lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) battery in a structural blade form factor - on 29 March 2020, first deployed in the BYD Han EV (July 2020), the first mass-produced vehicle built on the pack.

By the early 2020s the PLA Navy had become the world's largest navy by hull count (battle-force ships) - independent analysts date the crossover to around 2015, with PLAN battle-force ships (~350) exceeding the US Navy (~290). By TONNAGE, however, the US Navy remains substantially larger - a gap of roughly 3 million tons - driven by 11 nuclear supercarriers and a larger nuclear-submarine force. China leads in ship numbers; the US leads in aggregate displacement and per-ship capability.
SpaceX begins deploying Starlink, the first large low-Earth-orbit satellite-internet constellation.
SpaceX Crew Dragon flies the first commercial crewed orbital mission, restoring US human launch capability.
The first mRNA vaccines (COVID-19) are developed and authorized at record speed.

2021.claim: China's Tianwen-1 mission lands the Zhurong rover on Mars.
NASA's Ingenuity performs the first powered, controlled flight on another planet.

2022.claim: China completes the Tiangong space station in orbit.
The James Webb Space Telescope returns its first images, the most powerful space observatory ever.
The National Ignition Facility achieves fusion ignition with net energy gain from the reaction.
The CHIPS and Science Act commits large federal funding to reshore semiconductor manufacturing and research.
The Inflation Reduction Act enacts the largest US federal investment in clean energy and climate.
OpenAI releases ChatGPT, triggering mass adoption of generative AI.

2023.claim: China becomes the world's largest motor-vehicle exporter, led by electric vehicles.
In calendar year 2023 the United States became the world's largest exporter of liquefied natural gas, averaging 11.9 Bcf/d and surpassing Australia and Qatar (each about 10.1-10.5 Bcf/d).

2024.claim: Chang'e 6 returns the first samples ever collected from the far side of the Moon.

As of 2024 China accounted for roughly 69% of world rare-earth MINE production, and a materially higher share of rare-earth REFINING/separation - the distinction being the point: refining is more concentrated than mining.

China's 'Big Fund III' (Phase III of the National Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund) is incorporated on 24 May 2024 with about 344 billion yuan (~$47.5 billion) of registered capital - the largest of the three state chip funds - to finance domestic semiconductor self-sufficiency.
SpaceX catches a returning Starship booster with its launch tower, a step toward rapid full reuse.
Nvidia's AI accelerators drive it to briefly become the world's most valuable company, marking US dominance in AI hardware.

By late 2024 TSMC's Fab 21 in Phoenix, Arizona began high-volume manufacturing of 4-nanometre-class (N4) logic chips - the first leading-edge (sub-5nm) semiconductor production on US soil - confirmed by the US Commerce Department in January 2025.

Following the December 2022 first fusion ignition, the US National Ignition Facility repeatedly reproduced net-energy-gain fusion, reaching a record 5.2 MJ yield from 2.2 MJ of laser input (target gain about 2.3) on 10 February 2024 - establishing repeatability, not a single shot.

2025.claim: DeepSeek releases a competitive large language model at a fraction of typical training cost, jolting the global AI industry.
CATL unveiled its Naxtra sodium-ion battery brand on 21 April 2025, and in September 2025 Naxtra became the first sodium-ion power battery to pass China's GB 38031-2025 safety standard.

China commissioned its third aircraft carrier, Fujian (Type 003), on 5 November 2025 - its first carrier with electromagnetic catapults (the first outside the US Navy so equipped). It is commissioned but, per independent naval analysts, working up to full operational capability over the following years.
OpenAI released GPT-5 on 7 August 2025; independent evaluations reported 74.9% on SWE-bench Verified and 88.4% on GPQA Diamond.

On 26 August 2025 SpaceX's Starship Flight 10 completed the vehicle's first successful in-space payload deployment (eight Starlink mass simulators) and a controlled splashdown - its first fully successful upper-stage mission.

2026.claim: Moonshot AI releases Kimi K3 (unveiled 16 July 2026, open weights 27 July 2026), a 2.8-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that reached #1 on the independent LMArena Frontend Code Arena and rated the strongest open-weight model on Artificial Analysis - while trailing the leading US closed models (Claude Fable 5, GPT-5.6) on the aggregate index.

living_spec.title: A century of living standards — what the systems delivered · US above / China below · own scale per strip
living_spec.aria: Figure VI, A century of living standards: five human-development series (life expectancy, GDP per capita, infant mortality, schooling, urbanization) as thin US-above / China-below strips on the shared 1926-2026 axis, each on its own scale. Convergence is real and large, but the income level gap remains; every Chinese value before ~1980 is estimate-class.
living_spec.caption: Figure VI - a century of living standards (context-class; no corpus rows). Five human-development outcomes, US above / China below, each on its own scale. --- THE CONVERGENCE IS REAL AND LARGE: China closed a gap that in 1950 was civilizational - life expectancy 43.8 to ~78 years, infant mortality ~195 to ~5 per 1,000, mean schooling ~1.8 to ~9 years, urbanization ~11%% to ~65%% - and on two health measures China has now edged PAST the US (life expectancy since ~2021; infant mortality below the US by 2022, ~4.8 vs ~5.5). --- BUT IT IS NOT A RISE POSTER: the income LEVEL gap remains large - US real GDP per capita is ~3x China's on the Maddison basis drawn here (~4x on current-price PPP), schooling still trails ~4 years, and the US shows a genuine reversal, not merely China catching up. --- TWO DATED DIPS, the same no-silent-dips rule both ways: China's 1959-61 Great Leap famine (life-expectancy trough 33.4 in 1960; excess deaths carried as a range with both classes named - ~15M official vs ~30-45M demographic reconstructions - adjudicating neither), and the US 2015-2023 decline (opioid epidemic + COVID-19, CDC-documented; life expectancy ~78.8 to 76.4 by 2021, partial recovery to 77.5 in 2022). --- Every Chinese value before ~1980 is ESTIMATE-CLASS (reconstruction, not measurement), flagged per strip. Sources: UN WPP / IGME / WUP, Maddison, Barro-Lee. Selection: notes/living_series_selection.md.

capital_spec.caption: Figure Vb - the Capital System, three strips on one shared modern axis (~2014-2024). --- PRIVATE VC: annual venture-capital investment (PitchBook, log US$B) - China peaks $146B (2021) and collapses to $38B (2024, ~74%); the US falls ~41%. --- STATE-GUIDED CAPITAL (a drawn est. range, not a line): the China band's WIDTH is the gap between announced guidance-fund target (upper edge) and subscribed / committed capital (认缴, lower edge) - ~$1.4T / $585B in 2018 rising to ~$1.76T / $1.06T by 2024; subscribed is pledged, NOT paid-in cash and NOT deployed, so the true deployment gap is wider still. All figures trace to a single Chinese-origin vendor (Zero2IPO / 清科); the target line wobbles on scope (expired funds netted out), while new-fund formation fell ~25% in 2023 and ~37% underlying in 2024. China's Big Fund phases (through 2024) and the US SBIR / CHIPS comparators are discrete ticks - the US has no guidance-fund equivalent, so no US band is invented. --- IPO PROCEEDS: annual proceeds by venue (Renaissance / EY / KPMG, log US$B) - Chinese US-listings FROZE after DiDi (mid-2021), from ~$12.8B (2021) to ~$0.6B (2024), onshoring to the A-share market and Hong Kong. Private VC collapsed after 2021 while state-guided capital swelled; each band's width is measurement uncertainty, drawn not asserted. Sourcing: notes/founder_series_selection.md.

velocity_spec.headline: China leads velocity in ATOMS; the US leads in BITS and at the FRONTIER
velocity_spec.caption: Figure Vc - Velocity: four ways to be fast (OPEN-CAVEATED - a constructed comparison; the underlying numbers are real and sourced, but the choice of four dimensions and the US-vs-China pairing are authorial; re-choose them and the picture shifts). The honest spine: CHINA leads velocity in ATOMS, the US in BITS and at the FRONTIER - not one direction. --- DEPLOYMENT: electric-car share of new-car sales (IEA), China ~6 to 45%% in four years vs the US ~2 to 10%% (falling in 2025); China also added ~277 GW of solar in 2024 (US ~50) and runs ~48,000 km of high-speed rail (US ~0). But BITS invert: ChatGPT hit ~100M users in ~2 months and US AI-infrastructure capex (~$350B in 2025) dwarfs China's AI-cloud market (~$7B). --- ITERATION CADENCE: Chinese new-model dev cycles run ~20 months vs ~40 for legacy makers (AlixPartners/McKinsey) - but the US SETS the AI frontier and Chinese open models trail it ~4-8 months (Epoch/AISI/NIST); ships-more-often is a different axis from sets-the-frontier. --- TIME-TO-SCALE: exemplar dots, NOT a line - no honest paired median exists. China's 2010s cohort scaled fast (Xiaomi ~1.5yr, DiDi ~2yr), but SHEIN took ~11yr and the US 2023-25 AI cohort is now fastest (xAI ~$24B in ~14 months). --- CUTTHROAT: ~487 Chinese EV makers (2018) to ~129 (2025) to ~15 viable by 2030 (AlixPartners), only 3 profitable; the US concentrates early instead (Uber+Lyft ~99%%, Google ~90%%). The same selection forged BYD/CATL/DJI AND is now called 'involution' - a ~$69B EV price-war revenue wipe, 35 months of negative PPI, a state 'anti-involution' campaign. Full rubric + sources: notes/velocity_selection.md.
